original_question: Does there exist an infinite word over a three-letter alphabet in which every abelian square has length exactly 2? Equivalently, is there an infinite ternary word containing no abelian square of length greater than two, so that the only possible abelian square types are the one-letter doubles aa, bb, and cc?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 0.3 in the unnumbered section "The minimum numbers of distinct and non-equivalent abelian squares in words": the existence of an infinite ternary word containing no abelian square factors of length greater than two. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1802.04481))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s target very closely: it asks about an infinite ternary word, excludes all abelian square factors of total length greater than 2, and correctly identifies the surviving length-2 cases as the trivial doubles aa, bb, and cc. This is essentially the same problem as the paper’s official formulation of Mäkelä’s conjecture, just written more explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1802.04481))
missing_details: Make the paper’s definition of an abelian square explicit: a contiguous factor xy with |x|=|y| and identical Parikh vectors (equivalently, y is a permutation of x).
Clarify that "length greater than two" refers to the total length of the abelian-square factor, not its half-length or period.
State the ambient alphabet concretely as a ternary alphabet, e.g. {0,1,2} (or equivalently any 3-letter alphabet).
Use the paper’s scope phrase "infinite ternary word" rather than only "an infinite word over a three-letter alphabet."
Avoid implying that all of aa, bb, cc must occur; the conjecture only requires that no longer abelian square occur.
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite ternary word w over {0,1,2} such that no contiguous factor of w of the form xy with |x|=|y| and Parikh(x)=Parikh(y) has total length greater than 2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1802.04481))
justification: The draft is targeting Mäkelä’s conjecture exactly. The paper’s official statement is the shorter form "There exist infinite ternary words containing no abelian squares of length greater than two," and the only hidden notation needed to make it stand-alone is the preliminarily defined notion of abelian square via Parikh vectors. The nearby discussion and the appendix, which mention finite ternary words with no abelian squares other than 00, 11, and 22, confirm the intended concrete reading, but the formal target in the paper is Conjecture 0.3 itself and should not be broadened beyond that. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1802.04481))
